text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000112's 99215 rate is elevated across every complexity tier, but the small set of returned charts supports the billed levels, so the evidence does not yet separate upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs roughly double the all-provider share in every condition-count tier, including 5+ conditions, so panel complexity alone does not explain the excess. Only a small fraction of the 99215s fall on 0–1-condition patients. Against that, all 11 documented 99215s were supported, including C0062129 (a single-condition hypertension patient documented at high MDM), and the note checks are mostly clean. The documentation, though, covers about 2% of claims and cannot settle a pattern this large. Two cautions apply: the 99214 below-billed rate (C0063394, C0063490, both low MDM with no time recorded) is above the peer rate, and about a fifth of notes show repeated visit times. That repeated-time pattern, with no audit trail received, leaves open templated or cloned notes that could make documentation simply match billing. A reviewer should first request a larger chart sample weighted toward 99215s on low-complexity patients (for example C0062089, C0063125 and C0063236), and obtain audit trails to test whether the time and MDM entries reflect actual visit work."}
